question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The new software update B. He is highly allergic C. Neither the students nor the teacher || Column 2: D. to dairy products like milk and cheese. E. was present in the classroom. F. improves the battery life significantly. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-F match karta hai kyunki 'software update' ek subject hai jiska action 'improves' (verb) hai. B-D match hota hai kyunki 'allergic' ke baad fixed preposition 'to' lagta hai. C-E mein 'Neither...nor' ke rule ke hisaab se verb nearest subject (the teacher - singular) ke according 'was' aayega.
trick: Fixed preposition check karo. 'Allergic' ke baad hamesha 'to' aata hai, isse direct B-D match mil jayega aur options eliminate ho jayenge.
tip: Neither...nor mein verb hamesha paas wale subject (second subject) ke according lagta hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The book on the table B. I am looking forward C. Unless you work hard || Column 2: D. to meeting you next week. E. belongs to the library. F. you will not pass the exam. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-E sahi hai kyunki subject 'The book' (singular) hai, isliye verb 'belongs' aayega. B-D mein 'looking forward to' ek fixed phrasal verb hai jiske baad gerund (v+ing) aata hai. C-F ek conditional sentence hai, 'Unless' condition dikhata hai aur F uska result hai.
trick: 'Looking forward to' wale phrase ko dhundo. Iske baad hamesha V1+ing (gerund) lagta hai, isliye B-D sabse asaan match hai.
tip: 'Unless' wale part mein negative word (not) use nahi hota.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The police officer asked B. She usually drinks coffee C. Although he is rich || Column 2: D. but today she is having tea. E. he is very miserly. F. where I was going so late. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-F indirect speech hai; 'asked' ke baad wh-word (where) as a connector kaam karta hai. B-D mein habit aur temporary action ka contrast hai ('usually' vs 'today'). C-E mein 'Although' contradiction show karta hai, yani rich hone ke bawajood kanjoos (miserly) hai.
trick: Sentence start mein 'Although' dekho. Ye opposite ideas ko connect karta hai, isliye 'rich' ke sath negative trait 'miserly' (C-E) match hoga.
tip: Although aur Though ke sath kabhi 'but' ka use nahi karte, comma ya 'yet' lagate hain.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. As soon as the rain stopped B. He accused his neighbor C. The price of vegetables || Column 2: D. of stealing his bicycle. E. we went out to play. F. has increased drastically this month. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-E sequence of events dikhata hai; barish rukne ke turant baad khelne gaye. B-D mein 'accused' verb hai jiske sath hamesha fixed preposition 'of' lagta hai. C-F mein subject 'The price' (singular) hai, isliye helping verb 'has' aayega.
trick: 'Accused' ke turant baad 'of' preposition aata hai. Column 2 mein 'of' se shuru hone wala option D hai, toh B-D confirm ho gaya.
tip: Crime ke context mein 'accused' hamesha 'of' preposition leta hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. Not only did he buy a car B. The jury has given C. She prevented me || Column 2: D. from entering the restricted area. E. but he also bought a bike. F. its unanimous verdict today. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-E mein 'Not only... but also' ka correlative conjunction pair follow hua hai. B-F mein 'The jury' collective noun ki tarah act kar raha hai ('unanimous' yani ekmat), isliye singular verb 'has' aur pronoun 'its' laga hai. C-D mein 'prevented' ke baad 'from' preposition aata hai.
trick: Conjunction pairs yaad rakho. 'Not only' dikhte hi Column 2 mein 'but also' dhundo. A-E direct match hai.
tip: 'Prevent', 'prohibit', 'abstain' ke baad hamesha 'from + V1+ing' lagta hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. Scarcely had I reached the station B. He deals mainly C. The number of attendees || Column 2: D. in electronic goods and appliances. E. when the train left the platform. F. is expected to cross one thousand. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-E ek grammar rule hai; 'Scarcely/Hardly' ke sath conjunction 'when' lagta hai. B-D mein business ya trade ke liye phrasal verb 'deal in' use hota hai. C-F mein 'The number of' singular subject hota hai, isliye singular verb 'is' aayega.
trick: 'Deal in' (business karna) aur 'Deal with' (person/situation ko handle karna) ka difference yaad rakho. Yahan goods hai toh 'in' aayega.
tip: 'Scarcely' aur 'Hardly' hamesha 'when' pair ke sath aate hain, 'than' nahi.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The child is afraid B. No sooner did the bell ring C. Bread and butter || Column 2: D. than the students rushed out. E. is my favorite breakfast. F. of the dark room. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-F mein 'afraid' adjective hai jiske sath fixed preposition 'of' use hota hai. B-D ek grammar rule hai jisme 'No sooner' ke sath 'than' lagta hai. C-E mein 'Bread and butter' ek single dish/concept ko represent karte hain, isliye singular verb 'is' lagta hai.
trick: B mein 'No sooner' dekho. Iska pair hamesha 'than' hota hai, jo Column 2 ke option D mein hai. B-D 100% correct hai.
tip: 'Bread and butter' jab ek meal ko denote kare toh verb singular (is) aata hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. One of my best friends B. She prides herself C. If it rains tomorrow || Column 2: D. on her excellent cooking skills. E. we will cancel the picnic. F. lives in London. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-F mein 'One of' ke baad plural noun (friends) aata hai, lekin actual subject 'One' (singular) hai isliye verb 'lives' aayega. B-D mein 'prides' jab verb hota hai toh reflexive pronoun (herself) aur preposition 'on' leta hai. C-E Type 1 conditional sentence hai.
trick: Subject-verb agreement check karo. 'One of + plural noun' hamesha singular verb leta hai. A-F mein 'lives' singular verb hai.
tip: 'Pride' jab verb ho toh uske baad 'on' preposition aata hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The man whose car was stolen B. I prefer reading books C. Every boy and every girl || Column 2: D. to watching movies on TV. E. has filed a police complaint. F. was given a small gift. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-E complete context hai jahan ek relative clause (whose car...) main verb 'has filed' se judta hai. B-D mein 'prefer' ke sath comparison ke liye 'to' preposition aata hai ('than' nahi). C-F mein 'Every' word hamesha singular verb (was) leta hai chahe 'and' kyu na laga ho.
trick: 'Prefer' word milte hi Column 2 mein 'to' dhundo. Compare karne ke liye 'prefer... to...' use hota hai. B-D seedha match hai.
tip: 'Every' se jude huye do subjects hamesha singular verb lete hain.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The principal congratulated him B. A large number of students C. It is high time || Column 2: D. on his brilliant success. E. you started studying seriously. explanation: A-D mein 'congratulated' verb ke sath fixed preposition 'on' aata hai. B-F mein 'A large number of' ek plural subject hai jiske sath plural verb 'are' lagta hai. C-E ek specific grammar rule hai; 'It is high time' ke baad hamesha subject + V2 (Past Simple) aata hai.
trick: 'It is high time' wale phrase ko dekho. Iske baad hamesha Past Indefinite (V2) tense aata hai (started). Isliye C-E match hoga.
tip: 'A number of' plural verb leta hai, 'The number of' singular verb leta hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. He was completely absorbed B. The furniture in this room C. Had he driven carefully || Column 2: D. he would have avoided the accident. E. in reading the mystery novel. F. is made of teak wood. || Question: Which of the following represents the correct combination?
explanation: A-E mein 'absorbed' ke baad hamesha 'in' preposition lagta hai. B-F mein 'furniture' uncountable noun hai, isliye iske sath singular verb 'is' aayega. C-D ek Type 3 conditional (unreal past) sentence hai jisme 'Had + V3' ke sath 'would have + V3' use hota hai.
trick: Uncountable noun ka rule yaad rakho. 'Furniture' ka plural 'furnitures' nahi hota aur ye humesha singular verb (is) leta hai. B-F direct match.
tip: 'Had + subject + V3' aane par next clause mein 'would have + V3' lagta hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. My father insisted B. The scenery of Kashmir C. explanation: A-F mein 'insisted' ke sath 'on' preposition lagta hai aur uske baad possessive case (my) + gerund (going) aata hai. B-D mein 'scenery' uncountable noun hai isliye singular verb 'is' hai. C-E mein 'as if' (unreal condition) ke baad subject ke sath humesha 'were' lagta hai.
trick: 'As if' (jaise ki) imagination show karta hai. Imaginary sentences mein har subject (he/she/I) ke sath 'were' lagta hai. C-E match hoga.
tip: 'Insist' ke baad hamesha 'on' preposition aata hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The passengers refrained B. Let us discuss C. explanation: A-E mein 'refrained' (parhez karna) ke sath 'from' preposition lagta hai. B-D mein 'discuss' ek transitive verb hai jiske turant baad object 'the matter' aata hai ('about' nahi lagta). C-F mein 'Either...or' hone par verb paas wale subject ('he') ke according 'is' lagta hai.
trick: 'Discuss' ke sath koi preposition (jaise 'about') nahi lagta. Column 2 mein bina preposition wala direct object 'the matter' hai (B-D).
tip: Either...or aur Neither...nor mein verb second subject se agree karta hai.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. He died B. The teacher ordered the students C. tip: Kisi bimari se death hone par hamesha 'died of' lagaya jata hai.

tip: Time duration ('past ten years') batane ke liye hamesha 'for' ka use karein.

question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. The patient had died B. The blind man was accompanied C. question: Direction: Match the statements in Column 1 with those in Column 2 to form meaningful sentences. || Column 1: A. We should abide B. The climate of Pune C.
